automatic.label: Choose method automatically
automatic.summary: Picks a method that works on your network

conditions.hint: Helps the automatic choice start with a method that fits.

summary.obfuscated_udp: Disguised UDP for networks that block WireGuard
summary.tcp_fallback: Last resort when UDP is blocked
summary.quic: Looks like HTTP/3 web traffic on UDP

unsupported.owner_one: {{methods}} needs a newer version of the server software. Update the VPS to use it.
unsupported.owner_other: {{methods}} need a newer version of the server software. Update the VPS to use them.
unsupported.member_one: {{methods}} needs a newer version of the server software. Ask the Owner to update the VPS.
unsupported.member_other: {{methods}} need a newer version of the server software. Ask the Owner to update the VPS.

kill_switch.label: Kill switch
kill_switch.summary: Blocks internet if the VPN drops, until you disconnect
kill_switch.nextConnection: Saved, but not active yet. It turns on when you reconnect; until then, traffic isn’t blocked if the VPN drops.

automatic_reconnect.label: Automatic reconnect
automatic_reconnect.summaryAndroid: Retries if the connection drops. Applies immediately.
automatic_reconnect.info: When off, a dropped connection stays down until you reconnect. The kill switch keeps blocking either way.
automatic_reconnect.infoAndroid: When off, a dropped connection stays down until you reconnect. Switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data still gets one reconnect try.

android.label: Block connections without VPN
android.summary: Always-on VPN and blocking are set in Android. If blocking is on, internet stays blocked after you disconnect.

notes.selectedRoutes: Only your selected routes and system DNS use the VPN.
notes.windowsApps: Windows app routing needs the kill switch on and local network access off.
notes.launchedApps: Launched apps are blocked whenever the VPN is down; other apps use your normal network.

routing.title: Traffic routing

full_tunnel.label: Full tunnel
full_tunnel.summary: All internet traffic uses the VPN

selected_routes.label: Selected routes
selected_routes.summary: Only the IP ranges you list use the VPN

selected_applications.label: Selected apps
selected_applications.summaryAndroid: Choose which apps use the VPN
selected_applications.summaryWindows: Only the apps you choose use the VPN
selected_applications.summaryLinux: Only apps launched from SirinVPN use the VPN

routing.unsupported: App routing isn’t available on this device. Selected routes still work.
routing.unsupportedWindows: App routing is unavailable because its Windows driver isn’t running. Reinstall or update SirinVPN to restore it.
routing.windowsKillSwitch: Windows app routing needs the kill switch on. Turn it on in Connection settings before connecting.

android.blockNote: If Block connections without VPN is on, apps that don’t use the VPN have no internet.

routes.label: IP ranges (CIDR), one per line
routes.hint: Up to {{max}} ranges. System DNS always uses the VPN.
routes.empty: Add at least one range. With none, no traffic would use the VPN.
routes.invalid: Not a network in CIDR form, such as 198.51.100.0/24: {{routes}}

localNetwork.label: Allow local network
localNetwork.summary: Reach printers and other local devices outside the VPN
localNetwork.summaryLaunched: Lets launched apps reach devices on your local network
localNetwork.summaryWindows: Turn this off: Windows app routing needs local network access off

launcher.legend: Launch an app in the VPN
launcher.summaryLinux: Only apps you launch here use the VPN. Close any open copies first.
launcher.summaryWindows: Apps you choose here use the VPN. Close any open copies first.
launcher.infoLinux: Choose a native program. Flatpak and Snap apps, and apps that rely on a background service, may not work.
launcher.infoWindows: Choose a .exe on a local drive, and add each app that uses the network; helpers and services aren’t added for you. Selected apps can’t use IPv6, and system DNS goes through the VPN.
launcher.notReady: Save Selected apps and connect to this server to launch apps.
launcher.chooserError: Couldn’t open the file chooser. Enter the path instead.

arguments.label: One argument per line
arguments.hint: No quotes needed, even with spaces. Arguments aren’t saved.

launcher.safetyLinux: Launched apps never use the internet outside the VPN, even with the kill switch off. After you disconnect, they stay open but offline.
launcher.safetyWindows: Selected apps stay blocked outside the VPN if it drops or is paused. Disconnecting unblocks them and clears the selection.
launcher.exited: {{name}} exited right away. If it was already open, close it and try again.
launcher.launchError: Couldn’t launch the app in the VPN.
launcher.needsProgram: Enter a program or choose one with Browse.

mtu.title: Packet size (MTU)

automatic.label: Automatic packet size
automatic.summary: Measures and adjusts the packet size while connected

manual.label: Manual MTU
manual.hint: {{min}}–{{max}} bytes. Obfuscated UDP uses at most {{obfuscatedMax}} and QUIC at most {{quicMax}}.
manual.invalid: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
manual.invalidIpv6: With IPv6 on, enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.

mtu.notConnected: Connect to measure the packet size.
mtu.unsupported: Packet size can’t be measured until this device’s VPN component is updated. Review it in General settings under Local VPN component.

outcome.pending: Waiting to measure the packet size.
outcome.smaller: A smaller packet size was measured and will be applied.
outcome.manual: A recommendation is ready. Your manual MTU stays in use.
outcome.noReply: The server didn’t answer the measurement. The current MTU stays in use.
outcome.noUsable: Large packets don’t get through on this network. Try {{tls}} or {{tcp}}.
outcome.applyFailed: Couldn’t apply the measured size. MTU stays at {{value}} bytes.

selection.pending: Waiting for the first quality check.
selection.observing: Measured inside the VPN, not a speed test.
selection.waiting_for_idle: Will compare connection methods when traffic is idle.
selection.selected: Using the best connection method measured.
selection.icmp_unavailable: The server didn’t answer quality checks, so latency and loss are unavailable.
selection.protection_required: Turn on the kill switch to let SirinVPN compare connection methods.

reason.confirmed_failure: Switched connection method after the previous one failed.
reason.quality_improvement: Switched to a consistently better connection method.
reason.rollback: Kept the current connection method; the alternative didn’t connect.

startup.otherServer: Saved, but another server is connected now. Connect to this server to use it at startup.
startup.inactive: Saved, but not active yet. Select Connect and activate to turn it on.
startup.active: Connects to this server when this device starts.
startup.unconfirmed: The startup service is on, but it isn’t set to this server yet.

saveBar.pending: Saved for your next connection. Current connection: {{differences}}.
saveBar.invalid: Fix the highlighted values to save.

preferences.saved: Connection preferences saved. They apply from your next connection.
preferences.saveError: Couldn’t save. Your previous preferences are still in place.
